title: Flow Cytometry Immunophenotyping of Human Antigen-Specific T Cells
author: Rotta, Achille, et al.
materials: BD Horizon™ V500-C mouse anti-human CD8
BD Pharmingen™ PE mouse anti-human CCR7
BD Horizon™ BV786 mouse anti-human CD45RA
BD Horizon™ BV421 rat anti-human CXCR5
BD Pharmingen™ APC mouse anti-human CD137
BD Pharmingen™ PE-Cy™7 mouse anti-human CD69
BD Pharmingen™ FITC mouse anti-human IFNγ
BD Horizon™ BV711 mouse anti-human IL-2
BD Pharmingen™ Alexa Fluor™ 700 mouse anti-human TNF-α
BD Pharmingen™ purified NA/LE mouse anti-human CD3
BD Pharmingen™ purified NA/LE mouse anti-human CD28
BD Cytofix/Cytoperm™ Plus Fixation/Permeabilization Solution Kit
Timing: 1 h (the day before the experiment)

steps.title: Reconstitute Spike peptide pools
steps.instruction: The day before the experiment (≈1 h), remove each lyophilized Spike peptide pool (S, S1, S+) from –20 °C, warm to 18‑25 °C, add 200 µL sterile distilled water with a P200 pipette, vortex briefly, aliquot 5 µL into clearly labeled tubes, and store aliquots at –80 °C; keep the three pools separate to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Prepare viability stain stock
steps.instruction: The day before the experiment, retrieve the BD Horizon™ Fixable Viability Stain 575V vial from –80 °C, warm to 18‑25 °C, add 340 µL cell‑culture‑grade DMSO, vortex until fully dissolved, aliquot either 2 µL or 5 µL into labeled tubes, store at –20 °C, and discard any aliquot more than 90 days after preparation.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 2 µL or 5 µL into labeled tubes.

steps.title: Make viability working solution
steps.instruction: Dilute each viability‑stain aliquot 1:100 in staining buffer (e.g., PBS + 2 % FBS); use 10 µL of the diluted solution per sample. A 2 µL undiluted aliquot stains up to 20 samples, while a 5 µL aliquot stains up to 50 samples. Use the diluted solution immediately after thawing.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL diluted stain to each sample.
Calculate number of samples per aliquot (2 µL → 20; 5 µL → 50).

steps.title: Thaw and aliquot PBMCs
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw frozen PBMCs, count viable cells, and divide each donor sample into three equal aliquots of 1 × 10⁶ cells for positive control, negative control, and test conditions.

steps.title: Stimulate PBMCs with peptide pools
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate Spike peptide pool (S, S1, or S+) to each test aliquot at the recommended concentration, incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 24 h; after the first 4 h add Brefeldin A (protein transport inhibitor) to all tubes and continue incubation to the full 24 h.

substeps.instruction: Add peptide pool to test aliquot.

steps.title: Wash cells post‑stimulation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, and wash twice with staining buffer (e.g., PBS + 2 % FBS).

steps.title: Surface and viability staining
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in staining buffer, add 10 µL of the diluted viability dye per sample, add surface antibodies (CD45RA, CCR7, CXCR5, etc.) as per panel, and incubate 20 min at 4 °C protected from light.

substeps.instruction: Incubate 20 min at 4 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Fix and permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Fix cells with a fixation solution (e.g., 4 % paraformaldehyde) for 10 min at room temperature, wash, then permeabilize with the appropriate permeabilization buffer (e.g., saponin‑based) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Intracellular staining
steps.instruction: Add intracellular antibodies against CD137, CD69, IFN‑γ, TNF‑α, and IL‑2 to the permeabilized cells, incubate 30 min at 4 °C in the dark, then wash and resuspend in acquisition buffer.

substeps.instruction: Incubate 30 min at 4 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Acquire flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Run each sample on a flow cytometer, collecting at least 150 000 live singlet lymphocyte events; acquisition may be performed the same day or the following day after staining.

substeps.instruction: Collect ≥150 000 live singlet events per sample.

steps.title: Calculate stimulation index
steps.instruction: For each subset (AIM+ CD4+, cytokine‑producing AIM+ CD4+, AIM+ Tfh CD4+, AIM+ CD8+, cytokine‑producing AIM+ CD8+), compute the percentage of total CD4+ or CD8+ cells; calculate Stimulation Index = (% in stimulated)/( % in unstimulated). Classify a sample as a responder if the stimulated sample contains ≥20 AIM+ events and the Stimulation Index is ≥3.

substeps.instruction: Apply responder criteria (≥20 events and Index ≥3).

description: The following protocol describes steps for flow cytometry detection and immunophenotyping of human antigen-specific T cells recognizing SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein. It is based on the intracellular evaluation of activation induced markers CD137 and CD69 following overnight incubation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) with Spike protein peptide pool. Activation is assessed on live singlet CD3+ CD4+ and CD3+ CD8+ T lymphocytes which are also evaluated for intracellular accumulation of IFN-γ, TNF-α and IL-2 cytokines. Surface staining of CD45RA and CCR7 is used to describe the T cell maturation curve and the CXCR5 chemokine receptor, evaluated on live CD3+ CD4+ CD45RA- populations, is used to capture T helper follicular cells. To develop the protocol, frozen PBMCs from SARS-CoV-2 reactive samples were used, being reactivity induced by vaccination, natural infection, or both; but fresh PBMCs may also be used. Each sample is divided into three aliquots of 106 PBMCs/each as positive control, negative control, and test. Incubation with Spike peptide pools is done overnight taking 24 h, and protein transport inhibitor Brefeldin A is added after the first 4 h. Following incubation, cells are washed and stained for surface markers and viability, being then fixed, permeabilized and stained for intracellular markers and cytokines. Flow cytometry acquisition of 150,000 live singlet lymphocytes / sample can be done the same day of the staining or the following day. A major challenge in optimizing this protocol was identifying markers and conditions suitable for simultaneous AIM testing and intracellular Th1 cytokine detection for the characterization of antigen specific polyfunctional T cells.
